also: better the devil you know than the devil you don’t

terms.gloss: a bad thing you know is the best kind
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 63: nōta mala rēs optumast
terms.comment: One old man’s answer to another who has proposed, in jest, that they exchange wives: keep yours as you got her; with one he did not know he would not know what to do.

phrases.latin: nōta mala rēs optumast. Nam ego nunc sī ignōtam capiam, quid agam nesciam.
phrases.english: a known evil is the best evil. For if I took on one I didn’t know now, I shouldn’t know what to do.

sources: Lewis & Short: notus
